item.title: kb: close the audit gaps
item.description:
Everything the 2026-09-25 audit of `cli/kb-cli`, kb-js, kb-mcp and the Knowledge extension found against `specs/index-api.md` and `specs/index-ui.md`, minus what the single-store change (no `~/.kb`) already fixed.

- The spec was rebuilt from transcripts after the repo loss, so it may have drifted from the original design; check with the user when a ticket leans on a spec detail that looks off.

item.title: kb_get include:["links"] returns no links
item.description:
`kb get D-n --include links --json` emits `links: {outgoing, incoming}` (`cli/kb-cli/src/cmd_get.c`), but kb-js's `readDocumentRead` (`packages/kb-js/src/shape.ts`) never reads it and `KbDocumentRead` has no field for it. So `kb_get` with `include:["links"]` silently returns nothing.

**Done when:** `KbDocumentRead` carries `links?: { outgoing: KbLink[]; incoming: KbLink[] }` exactly when asked for, `readDocumentRead` reads it through the existing `readLink`, and a kb-js contract test against the real binary plus a kb-mcp test cover it.

item.title: Search hits omit scores.fused, and minScore filters raw BM25
item.description:
`cmd_search.c` computes the reciprocal-rank-fusion score (`fused[i].score`) but emits only `scores.bm25`, and its comment wrongly says only computed scores are emitted. `--min-score` is applied to raw BM25 inside `fts_search`, not to the fused score index-api §4 describes.

**Done when:** every hit carries `scores.fused`; `scores.vector` stays absent until semantic search exists (T in M-3); `minScore` is defined (and documented) against the fused score, or the spec says otherwise; e2e covers both.

item.title: Knowledge: a document's Refresh button runs a store-wide report
item.description:
The stale badge's refresh action in the document header (`webview/Document.tsx`) sends `{document}`; `src/host.ts` drops it and runs `kb refresh` over the whole store, which only reports and fetches nothing, then silently reloads the tab.

index-ui §3.1 wants a per-document refresh. The honest options: (a) re-read the document's source when it is a file (the locator is its path) and re-file it with `kb add`, (b) for a URL source, re-fetch through the extension's existing `fetchPage`, (c) otherwise say plainly that there is nothing to refresh from. Needs the source route from M-2 only if we want the CLI to own it.

**Done when:** the button refreshes that document (or explains why it cannot), shows the outcome, and never runs a store-wide command.

item.description:
`cmd_search.c` computes the reciprocal-rank-fusion score (`fused[i].score`) but emits only `scores.bm25`, and its comment wrongly says only computed scores are emitted. `--min-score` is applied to raw BM25 inside `fts_search`, not to the fused score index-api §4 describes.

**Done when:** every hit carries `scores.fused`; `scores.vector` stays absent until semantic search exists (T-11); `minScore` is defined (and documented) against the fused score, or the spec says otherwise; e2e covers both.

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S5 (git `6d4a5d0`).

- **`scores.fused`** is on every hit: the reciprocal-rank sum the list is ordered by (1/61 for the top hit of a single list). `vector` stays absent until the vector path runs.
- **`minScore`** stays a floor on the **bm25** score, applied **before** fusion — decided rather than changed. The fused score is 1/(k + rank): it says where a hit landed, not how well it matched (the best hit of a poor query scores the same as the best of a good one), so a floor on it would only be a second `k`. §4 and the code now say so.
- **e2e**: fused present on every hit, 1/61 at the top, hits in fused order; a floor between two hits' bm25 drops only the weaker, and fusion re-ranks the rest from the top. The old test asserted `fused` was absent — it encoded the bug.

Suites: C unit 2296, e2e 141, kb-js 102, kb-mcp 134 — all green; index-vscode 86/87 (only the known T-14 failure).

Left for T-11: kb-js reads an absent `scores.vector` as `0` (`readScores` in `shape.ts`), which blurs the absent-versus-zero distinction the CLI keeps. It only matters once vectors exist.

item.title: Knowledge: opening a search hit does not scroll to its heading in some documents

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S7 (git `bac99b9`).

- **Headings:** the chunk's heading (kept *as written* by the chunker) is brought to the heading *as shown* before its id is made — markdown inline code, emphasis, strikethrough, links, escapes and entities; HTML entities through the HTML renderer's own decoder. **Checked end to end** beyond the unit tests: real `kb` chunks of a markdown, an HTML and a C document, rendered through the real `Body` component (server-side React), all 9 land on an element that exists — before, 4 of the 6 headings and all 3 code chunks would have stayed at the top.

item.title: Forget a document or a source (DELETE /documents, /sources)

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S8 (git `d395dc9`).

- **Log:** `documents.jsonl` gains a `forget` record. The fold drops the document; its id and chunk range stay spent (never reused), links to it read `resolved: false`, and its blob waits for `kb compact`.
- **`kb forget D-n`** forgets one document; **`kb forget S-n`** a source with every document under it. One path (`forget_records`): documents first, then sources, then the keyword index rebuilt, all under one lock.
- **`kb collections delete <name> --with-documents`** forgets what the topic holds. Without the flag it still refuses with `collection_in_use` (now naming the flag) — forgetting a topic's contents is asked for by name. `rename --with-documents` is refused.
- **kb-js:** `forget(id)` → `{documents, sources, note}`, `deleteCollection(name, { withDocuments })`. Not an MCP tool (§9).
- **Knowledge:** a collection's Forget now forgets its documents, as its confirmation already promised, instead of being refused.

**Found and fixed on the way (pre-existing):** kb-js appended `--json` after a `--` separator, where kb read it as a positional — so **renaming or deleting a collection** from Knowledge and **searching for a dash-led query** (from Knowledge or agents) got a text answer kb-js could not parse. `--json` now goes in front of `--`.

Tests: C unit 2312, e2e 148 (7 new forget tests), kb-js 105 (forget and the collection delete against the real binary, the `--json` placement, key coverage for `forget`), kb-mcp 134, index-vscode 96/97 (only T-14), combined check green. Spec §7 notes the default refusal.

item.title: Forget a document or a source (DELETE /documents, /sources)
Source routes: sources list/show/refresh, and file ingest

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S9 (git `868092e`).

- **`kb sources [--collection C] [--kind K]`** lists sources; **`kb sources show S-n`** gives the source, its documents, and their **fetch history** (every `document` and `touch` record, oldest first — the fold only keeps the latest, so `doclog_fetches` reads them back).
- **`kb refresh S-n`** reads a **file** source again and re-indexes it only if the text changed (same document id, fresh chunk range). A **url** source is refused with `fetch_failed` (no HTTP client, §12.2 — re-file with `kb add --url`), an **inline** one with `usage` (nothing to read again). `kb refresh` without an id is still §5's report; mixing the two is refused.
- **`refile_document`** is now the one path by which an existing document is handed its text again — `kb add` and `kb refresh S-n` share it (a behaviour-preserving extraction; the whole suite passed before anything was added on top).
- **File ingest by locator** already existed as `kb add --file`; no directory walk, by design (T-12).
- **kb-js:** `sources()`, `source(id)`, `refreshSource(id)`; the key-coverage test checks `sources show` and each `sources` row against what the binary prints.
- **Knowledge:** the `kb:/S-n` page now reads `kb sources show`: kind, locator, last fetch, the documents, the fetch history newest first, and a Refresh action for file sources. Checked rendered in headless Chrome.

Tests: C unit 2312, e2e 153 (5 new), kb-js 107, kb-mcp 134, index-vscode 96/97 (only T-14), combined check green.

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S10 (git `e80b134`).

- `kb add` is split into **prepare** (kind, locator, mime, hash — refusable before any lock) and **ingest** (write one prepared document), so the single and the batch path are one path. The full suite passed on the restructure before batch was added.
- **`kb add --batch`** reads one JSON object a line on stdin (title, collection, content; url, mime, meta optional). The same locator twice in a batch is one document.
- **kb-js:** `addBatch(documents)`; `readAdded` shared with `add`.
- **kb-mcp:** `kb_add` is one batch call; a refusal returns `filed: 0` and says none were filed. Its description tells agents so. The guard now also forbids `forget` and `refreshSource` from the tools.

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S11 (git `a863dd9`).

- **CLI:** errors are `{ok:false, error, message, details?}`. A small `errdet` module holds one pending details object per process, **owned by a code**, so details recorded by a lower layer (the lock in `store_open`, staleness in `fts_open_store`) print only under that code and never ride on an unrelated error.
  - `store_locked` → `{store, pid}`
  - `collection_in_use` → `{collection, documents}`
  - `index_stale` → `{structures: ["keyword"], path}` / `{structures: ["chunks"], document}`; `kb status` carries it inline
  - `fetch_failed` → `{locator}`
  - `unsupported_mime` → `{mime}`: `kb add` (single and batch) now refuses anything not `text/*` or a text-like `application/*` (JSON, XML, YAML, TOML, JS, TS, shell, XHTML), before the store is opened.
  - `model_missing`'s `path` lands with T-10, when the embedder is actually built.
- **kb-js:** `KbError.details` (raw) and `detailsOf(code)`, typed per code in `KbErrorDetails` and shape-checked, so a mis-shaped object reads as null rather than a lie.
- **kb-mcp:** refusals pass `details` to the agent.
- **Knowledge:** delete asks the store first; an empty collection just goes, and one that holds documents is confirmed with the **store's** count from `collection_in_use` — not the row's count from the last refresh.
- **Spec §11** names the fields.

Tests: unit 2319, e2e 158, kb-js 110, kb-mcp 135, index-vscode 96/97 (T-14).

Done in lap session S12 (git `09bf272`). All seven:

- [x] **Source etag/status.** `kb add --etag` (and batch `etag`) records the ETag the caller's fetch saw; a source's `etag` is its newest document's, cleared when new text arrives without one. `status` is recorded: a refresh that cannot read the file marks it `fetch_failed` (once), and the next successful filing sets it back to `ok`. `kb sources --status S --q text`.

Done in lap session S13 (git `07cdcd8`).

- The spec's opening now says kb holds what was **read** (docs, papers, reference source at a pinned version), never the code being **written**, and why: that code is stale as soon as it is indexed, and grep and the LSP already answer it.

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S19 (git `3bd227d`).

- **`index/vectors.bin`**: one int8 vector per chunk, keyed by **chunk id**, with the model fingerprint. Chunk ids name one passage forever, so a stored vector stays right as long as the model does:
  - `kb add` and `kb rebuild` embed only chunks with no vector, and drop vectors whose chunks are gone;
  - `kb reindex` re-embeds everything;
  - `rebuild` reports `vectors: {kept, embedded, dropped}`; `reindex` reports the real `reembedded` count.
- **Speed:** a 375-token chunk took **7.3 s**. Two changes brought it to **0.58 s**:
  - `quant_matmul` dequantises each super-block once per sequence instead of once per token (3.6 s);
  - `plat_parallel` (pthreads / Win32) runs the matmul rows and the attention heads on every core.
  - A query takes about 16 ms to embed and about 35 ms end to end.
  - The vectors are **bit-identical** to the old single-threaded pass (hashes compared on three texts), so the llama.cpp comparison still holds.
- **Search:**
  - The default is **hybrid** whenever the store's vectors cover it under the model on disk; otherwise it is keyword, and `mode` in the response says which ran.
  - `--mode hybrid|semantic` refuses with `model_missing`, `model_mismatch`, or `index_stale` on `["vectors"]` with `missing: n`.
  - Both lists go to depth max(3k, 50), then RRF. A chunk found by both paths is one candidate with `matched: ["keyword","semantic"]`.
  - `scores.bm25` and `scores.vector` appear only for the paths that found the hit.
  - Text output shows kw / sem / kw+sem.
- **`kb status`** adds `index.vectors: {count, missing, current}`.
- **kb-js:** `KbScores.bm25` and `.vector` are optional, and `readScores` keeps an absent score absent (the comment on this ticket). One test had pinned the old zeros; it now pins absence.
- **e2e:** `make e2e` picks up the `.gguf` in the real `~/.kb/models` automatically (or `KB_TEST_MODEL`) and skips the model tests without one.
  - The model tests cover: hybrid by default with both scores; semantic ranking the bread note first for a query that shares no word with it; the collection filter; rebuild keeping and dropping vectors; and the missing-vector refusal, keyword fallback and re-embedding.

author: agent
body:
Done: `specs/artifacts.md` (lap session S20).

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S32.

Knowledge already had **Add URL**. It asks before fetching, fetches in the extension host, and files the page as it arrived (HTML is rendered as prose at read time, so the stored bytes stay the page's own). What it lacked, and now has:
- **The ETag.** Add URL files it (`kb add --etag`), so the source records it.
- **Conditional refresh.** A document's Refresh sends `If-None-Match` with the recorded ETag. A **304** re-files the stored text, which only moves `fetchedAt`. A changed page is re-indexed and its new ETag recorded.
- **Url sources.** On a url source's page, Refresh now works: it goes through the same fetch in the extension, since the CLI still has no network, and the answer has the shape the page already shows.
- **Plain failures.** An unreachable host is named with its error code ("Could not reach 127.0.0.1:1: ECONNREFUSED."), and a non-2xx says the status and that **nothing was filed**.

**Test:** a local HTTP server that honours `If-None-Match`, run against the real kb binary. It covers fetch and ETag, an unchanged refresh (with the conditional header checked), a changed page with its new ETag, a 500 that changes nothing, and an unreachable host. index-vscode: 99 pass.

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S33.

**Extractor decided: pdf.js (`pdfjs-dist` 6.3, Apache-2.0).** It is pure JavaScript, so there's nothing for the user to install and the vsix stays universal. An external tool like `pdftotext` would be one more thing to set up. It ships as its minified module and worker (1.8 MB) **beside** the bundle and is loaded with a real dynamic import, because it is ES modules that load their worker by relative path. The vsix is now 1.06 MB. Knowledge's dependency guard test names it with the reason, rather than being loosened.

- **Add Files** accepts PDFs. The text is filed as **Markdown**:
  - a `#` title (the PDF's own, or the file name) and its author;
  - one **`## Page N` section per page**, so the heading chunker splits on pages and **a search hit says which page it's on**;
  - lines and paragraphs rebuilt from baselines;
  - prose that would read as Markdown structure escaped.

  The locator is the PDF's path, and the meta records its page count and author.
- **Refresh** on a PDF document reads the file again and re-extracts it.
- **Tests:** 3 new, 102 in total. One takes a hand-built two-page PDF through pdf.js and the real kb binary: search finds page-2 text with heading "Page 2". That test also caught a paragraph-detection bug (upper median of gaps), which is fixed.
- **Checked the packaged vsix:** its pdf.js extracts text without the optional canvas module. The canvas warnings only concern rendering pages as images and will appear in the extension log.

Not done: scanned PDFs (images with no text layer) produce empty pages, because that would need OCR.

item.title: Board: archive
item.description:
Epics, milestones and tickets can be **archived**: hidden from lists, search, the sidebar and Kanban by default, and still readable by id. Archiving is reversible, and agents may do it (they still never delete).

**Design:**
- **Storage:** new `archive` / `unarchive` records in the same `.coboard/log.jsonl`, not a field on the item and not a second file.
  - Old readers ignore the new records, and an old writer's whole-item `put` cannot silently un-archive.
  - One file keeps a write atomic under the one lock, and keeps archived ids reserved so they are never reused.
- **Scope:** an item is hidden when it or anything above it (milestone, epic) is archived. Nothing is written to the children, so unarchiving the epic brings everything back.
- **Compatibility:** every existing API and MCP tool keeps its shape. New parameters are optional, the default excludes archived items (which changes nothing until something is archived), and archiving itself is new tools on top.

item.description:
Epics, milestones and tickets can be **archived**: hidden from lists, search, the sidebar and Kanban by default, and still readable by id. Archiving is reversible, and agents may do it (they still never delete).

- **Storage:** new `archive` / `unarchive` records in the same `.coboard/log.jsonl`, not a field on the item and not a second file.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S52, git 09eaadf.

- **`src/bpe.c`:**
  - NFC through vendored **utf8proc v2.10.0** (MIT, Unicode 16; `src/third_party/utf8proc`, with its tag, commit and license). Invalid UTF-8 becomes U+FFFD first.
  - The 116 **added tokens are split out first**, leftmost-longest, including the 2–24-space runs that code indentation becomes.
  - The GPT-2 split as a hand-written scanner, with the alternatives in order, `\s` as Oniguruma's Unicode White_Space, and categories from utf8proc.
  - GPT-2's byte alphabet, then merges by rank, with every occurrence of a pair merged left to right.
  - `[CLS] a [SEP]` and pairs `[CLS] q [SEP] p [SEP]`, with the passage cut first.
- **Exact:** kb's ids equal the Hugging Face tokenizer's on **651/651 files, 3,350,148 tokens**:
  - every tracked text file in this repository (docs, C, TypeScript, CSS, JSON, shell, Python);

Done in lap session S54. Commits: 28da2a6 (CLI) and 84f59b9 (kb-js, MCP, Knowledge view).

- **`kb add --dir D --collection C [--no-forget]`** files a folder as one `dir` source, with one document per file at its `path`. Spec §2.1 describes it.
  - It reads the folder the way git does: nested `.gitignore` files with git's full rules (negation, anchoring, dir-only, `**`), from the repository root down, plus `.git/info/exclude`. The rules were checked against `git check-ignore`.

item.description:

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S59, commit 26e867b.

**What kb does now:**
- **Split-then-merge (`syntax_cuts`):**
  - Siblings are grouped into units, with comments and attributes above a definition kept with it.
  - Units are merged while they fit 1,600 bytes.
  - A unit that doesn't fit is split along its children. A definition becomes the container; blocks and statements don't, so the path reads `fn > if (x) {`, not `fn > { > …`.
  - A small open chunk before a too-big unit goes into that unit's first piece, so a signature never stands alone.
  - A final pass merges pieces left over by a split.
  - Chunks tile the file from byte 0.
- **Headings:** `container > signature`, taken from the first definition-like node in the chunk. Definition-like is judged by whole words of the node type, so an assembler's `instruction` isn't taken for a `struct`.
- **Header line:** every code chunk is indexed and embedded under `title > heading` (the file, then the function) ahead of its text (`chunk_header`).
- **Choosing the grammar:** `doc_syntax` uses the document path, or the mime type for single files. TypeScript that won't parse is retried as TSX.
- **Fallback:** a file whose tree is more than 10% error is cut into line windows. Code without a grammar keeps the old line-based splitting.
- **Chunker version:** now `structural-2`, so stores built with structural-1 show "reindex owed".

**Tested per language on snapshots of real repository files** (`tests/fixtures/syntax/`): C (`gitignore.c`), TypeScript (`client.ts`), TSX (`Body.tsx`), JavaScript (`playground.mjs`) and Python (`convert.py`), plus Go, Rust and GNU-as fixtures.
- Every file is checked for tiling, size budget and headings.
- Named headings are checked, such as `export class Kb { > async addDir(...)`, `def main(): > …`, `impl<'a> Lexer<'a> { > fn ident(...)` and `kb_memchr:`.

item.description:

item.title: lap: intent and behavior, and commits that name each other
item.description:
A lap commit's single message becomes two required fields: **intent** (why the edit exists, shared by edits that serve one goal) and **behavior** (what this edit makes the code do, its own for every edit). `lap commit` refuses weak messages with simple word-overlap checks, prints the new commit's hash, and every command that takes a commit accepts a hash; a commit's text refers to another as `#<hash>`, which the UIs turn into links.

Why: one edit per commit is what makes large agent changes reviewable, but a single message invited the `(1/n) … (n/n)` pattern, where one reason was copied across fragments and each hunk stopped explaining itself. Splitting intent from behavior lets the shared part be shared honestly and makes each hunk say what it does.

**Decided**
- `-m` is removed outright; every command refuses flags it does not know (`unknown_flag`).
- lap is unreleased: the spec changes in place, with no version bump and no compatibility rules. A commit without both `intent` and `behavior` is malformed; `msg`-only commits are not read.
- This repository's log is converted once, in place, by a throwaway script (not a lap command): each `msg` becomes the `intent` with its `(i/n) ` prefix stripped, and `behavior` is the fixed string `The data of this field is not present`. Ids are kept; the hash chain is recomputed.
- Grouping by intent (in `rr` and the board) is display only: every hunk stays its own commit.
- No relationship types: "needs" or "fixes" are just words next to a `#hash`.
- lap stays single-developer: no branches, logs are never merged.

**Out of scope:** branches, the GitLab/GitHub mirror, lap suggesting links by reading code.

**Cutover:** the CLI, both extensions and the skills land together, with the log converted at the same time; the installed lap cannot read a converted log.

Where the draft spec is: the first comment on T-66.

item.description:

- **Model files** go in `~/.kb/models`. The user allowed writing them there, and nothing else under `~`.
- **Reference:** a throwaway Python venv (transformers, sentence-transformers) checks the C tokenizer, forward pass and reranker.
- **Languages:** C, TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Go, Rust, Assembly.

**Target:** hit@1 ≥ 0.80 on a benchmark of 150+ doc queries and 100+ code queries, with bootstrap intervals. The baseline is today's hit@1 0.63–0.67 on 30 doc queries.

item.title: lap status: skip unchanged files with a stat cache
lap: intent and behavior, and commits that name each other
item.description:
A lap commit's single message becomes two required fields: **intent** (why the edit exists, shared by edits that serve one goal) and **behavior** (what this edit makes the code do, its own for every edit). `lap commit` refuses weak messages with simple word-overlap checks, prints the new commit's hash, and every command that takes a commit accepts a hash; a commit's text refers to another as `#<hash>`, which the UIs turn into links.

Why: one edit per commit is what makes large agent changes reviewable, but a single message invited the `(1/n) … (n/n)` pattern, where one reason was copied across fragments and each hunk stopped explaining itself. Splitting intent from behavior lets the shared part be shared honestly and makes each hunk say what it does.

**Decided**
- `-m` is removed outright; every command refuses flags it does not know (`unknown_flag`).
- lap is unreleased: the spec changes in place, with no version bump and no compatibility rules. A commit without both `intent` and `behavior` is malformed; `msg`-only commits are not read.
- This repository's log is converted once, in place, by a throwaway script (not a lap command): each `msg` becomes the `intent` with its `(i/n) ` prefix stripped, and `behavior` is the fixed string `The data of this field is not present`. Ids are kept; the hash chain is recomputed.
- Grouping by intent (in `rr` and the board) is display only: every hunk stays its own commit.
- No relationship types: "needs" or "fixes" are just words next to a `#hash`.
- lap stays single-developer: no branches, logs are never merged.

**Out of scope:** branches, the GitLab/GitHub mirror, lap suggesting links by reading code.

**Cutover:** the CLI, both extensions and the skills land together, with the log converted at the same time; the installed lap cannot read a converted log.

Where the draft spec is: the first comment on T-66.

item.title: lap status: skip unchanged files with a stat cache

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S80 (L2740–L2780), git `df6154c`.

**Measured** on a byte-identical copy of typec (rsync -a, mtimes kept; 14,653 working files, 3 pending), nothing changed between runs:

| | cold | warm |
|---|---|---|
| before | 6.37 s | 1.39 / 1.44 s |
| after, first run (builds the cache) | — | 1.52 s |
| after | — | 0.43 / 0.36 / 0.35 s |

Output is byte-identical before and after. What remains (0.08 s user, 0.27 s sys) is the working-tree walk itself: readdir and one lstat per entry, about what `find` costs over the same tree.

**What changed**
- **Stat cache** `.lap/statcache` (new `statcache.c`): per tracked file last found clean, its size, mtime (ns where kept) and the index entry of its last commit (head). A walked tracked file whose stat and head match is not read. Keying on the head rather than on the shadow's stat means a commit invalidates the entry with no second stat.
- **No second stat:** `plat_walk` now hands each callback the lstat it already made (`PlatStat`; Windows fills it from the find data).
- **No shadow walk:** with an index, `status` merges the sorted walk against the index's live files (last commit not a delete); tracked files the walk did not see are the deletions. Without an index it walks the shadow store as before.
- **The reader exception** (spec): `status` writes the cache only when its entries changed, only under `plat_trylock` (non-blocking flock; one attempt on Windows), atomically (temp + rename), and only for files this run read and found clean.
- **Racy rule:** an entry is added only when the file's mtime is older than the run's start second.
- Spec: repository layout, cache contract (the exception named), and a Stat cache entry in the acceleration layer.

**Tests:** unit 1811/1811; e2e 89/89. New scenarios: entries only for settled clean files (a future-dated file is never cached); new bytes with the size and old mtime restored stay "clean" until the cache is deleted (which shows the file was not read); same-size and racy edits found; a commit's new head invalidates the entry; deletions found through the index and without it; no refresh while another process holds the lock (python3 holds it). The per-file cache-contract loop now deletes `statcache` too.

**Not verified:** the Windows paths (FILETIME conversion, `plat_trylock`) compile only in theory; no Windows build here. Measured on the copy, not in `/Users/praisethemoon/code/typec` itself, so nothing was written there.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S82 (L2781–L2792), git `74eec7a`.

- `lap commit … --dry-run` runs the same code as a commit up to the append: file and ignore checks, session gate, edit selection (`--edit`/`--lines`, `no_changes`, `multiple_edits`), the message checks against the session's previous behavior. Then it prints and stops.
- **A reader:** `repo_open(…, for_write = !dry)`, so no lock, no torn-tail cut, no `state.json` rewrite; counters are healed in memory, which is where the predicted id comes from.
- **Human:** `dry run, nothing written: would record L2 in S1`, then op, file, region (and `(forced)`), the intent and the behavior.
- **JSON:** `{"ok":true,"dry_run":true,"record":{…}}`, the record as `rec_encode` would write it with its `prev` removed, so no hash either.
- Spec (`lap commit` section), help, and the lap skill (both copies) document it.
- **Tests:** e2e 90/90. The new scenario checks: human and JSON output; no `prev`/`hash`; `message_too_short`, `behavior_repeats_intent`, `unknown_file`, `no_changes`, `multiple_edits`, `behavior_repeats_previous`; every file under `.lap/` byte-identical before and after (shasum); the predicted id equals the id the real commit then gets; with `state.json` removed and a torn tail appended, the dry run still predicts correctly and leaves both as they were.

author: claude
body:
**Widened by the user to the CLI too. Decided:**
- **Stored:** UTC, unchanged (log `ts`, JSON output).
- **CLI human output** (`log`, `search`, `rr`, `session list`): local time as `2026-09-27 11:36:48` (fixed year-month-day order, not the locale's). `lap show` adds the offset: `2026-09-27 11:36:48 +02:00`.
- **Filters** (`--since`/`--until`): a time with `Z` or an offset is taken as given; a zone-less time is local (`2026-09-27`, `2026-09-27 11:00`, `2026-09-27T11:00:00`), so anything copied from the output filters correctly. In the repeated hour when clocks go back, the first of the two moments is taken.
- **Editor views:** both `localTime` formatters print the locale's date, a space, and the time with seconds.
- Spec's timestamp paragraph says all of this.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S83 (L2796–L2816), git `00d1ea0`.

**CLI**
- `plat_ts_local` renders a stored UTC time in the machine's zone: `2026-09-27 11:36:48`. The offset (`+02:00`) is computed from the local fields read back as UTC, so it needs no `tm_gmtoff` and works on Windows.
- Used by `log` and `search` rows, `search --file --line` ("last touched by … (2026-09-27 11:46:59)"), `rr`'s span, and `show`, which adds the offset: `date: 2026-09-27 11:46:59 +02:00`.
- `plat_ts_parse` turns a filter time into a log timestamp: a date, or a date and time (`T` or space, seconds optional). `Z` or an offset (`+05:30`, `-0400`) is taken as given; zone-less is local; in the repeated hour the earlier moment wins; anything else is `bad_time`. `search --since/--until` convert both bounds before comparing. This also fixes date-only bounds, which the index's prefilter used to ignore.
- JSON and the log are unchanged (UTC ISO). The spec's timestamp paragraph says all of it.

**Editor views:** both `localTime` formatters print `09/27/2026 11:36:48 AM` (the locale's date, a space, time with seconds). Lap History's moved from `extension.ts` into `model.ts` so it can be tested.

**Tests**
- Unit 1828/1828. `test_time` sets `TZ`: UTC, Kolkata `+05:30`, New York in summer and winter, and Berlin parsing including 2026-10-25 02:30 → 00:30Z (the earlier moment).
- e2e 91/91. JSON is UTC; `TZ=Asia/Tokyo` shows `+09:00`; a time copied from `log` works in `--since` and `--until`; the same text under `TZ=UTC` matches nothing; `bad_time`.
- lap-vscode 37/37, coboard-vscode 36/36, each with a `localTime` test.

**Checked instead of rendered:** the author line lives in VS Code's native comment thread, not a webview, so it was printed from the built modules rather than rendered. Board: `L14562 · f10e721 @ 09/27/2026 11:36:48 AM claude:`; Lap History: `L14562 f10e721 @ 09/27/2026 11:36:48 AM claude:`.

**Not verified:** Windows builds.

item.title: lap: intent and behavior, and commits that name each other
item.description:
A lap commit's single message becomes two required fields: **intent** (why the edit exists, shared by edits that serve one goal) and **behavior** (what this edit makes the code do, its own for every edit). `lap commit` refuses weak messages with simple word-overlap checks, prints the new commit's hash, and every command that takes a commit accepts a hash; a commit's text refers to another as `#<hash>`, which the UIs turn into links.

Why: one edit per commit is what makes large agent changes reviewable, but a single message invited the `(1/n) … (n/n)` pattern, where one reason was copied across fragments and each hunk stopped explaining itself. Splitting intent from behavior lets the shared part be shared honestly and makes each hunk say what it does.

**Decided**
- `-m` is removed outright; every command refuses flags it does not know (`unknown_flag`).
- lap is unreleased: the spec changes in place, with no version bump and no compatibility rules. A commit without both `intent` and `behavior` is malformed; `msg`-only commits are not read.
- This repository's log is converted once, in place, by a throwaway script (not a lap command): each `msg` becomes the `intent` with its `(i/n) ` prefix stripped, and `behavior` is the fixed string `The data of this field is not present`. Ids are kept; the hash chain is recomputed.
- Grouping by intent (in `rr` and the board) is display only: every hunk stays its own commit.
- No relationship types: "needs" or "fixes" are just words next to a `#hash`.
- lap stays single-developer: no branches, logs are never merged.

**Out of scope:** branches, the GitLab/GitHub mirror, lap suggesting links by reading code.

**Cutover:** the CLI, both extensions and the skills land together, with the log converted at the same time; the installed lap cannot read a converted log.

Where the draft spec is: the first comment on T-66.

item.description:
On a fresh Windows clone of typec (only `.lap/log.jsonl` from git, `lap rebuild` failing, so no caches), `lap status` died asking `malloc` for 68,719,476,736 bytes.

Cause: `file_diff_load` → `shadow_from_log` (`cmd_common.c`) rebuilds a missing shadow by calling `idx_ready` (which loads the whole index) and, without an index, `rec_log_load` (the whole 34 MB log, parsed) — **once per file**, into the command's one arena, which frees nothing and doubles each new chunk. ~14,600 files × tens of MB → a 64 GiB chunk request.

Fix: load the index, or the log, at most once per command and reuse it for every file. Keep it valid only while the log has not changed size (a writer in the same command appends after reading).

**Done when:**
- `shadow_from_log` loads the index or the log once per command, however many files it is asked about;
- a reproduction (many files, caches deleted, `lap status`) is measured before and after (peak memory and time) in the closing comment;
- lap's unit and e2e suites pass, with an e2e case for status with every cache deleted over many files.

item.title: kb builds on Linux: tree-sitter finds its own unicode headers
item.description:
On Linux, building kb fails: `src/third_party/tree-sitter/lib/src/unicode/utf8.h:37: fatal error: unicode/umachine.h: No such file or directory`.

The vendored copy has the file (`lib/src/unicode/umachine.h`), but `utf8.h` includes it as `"unicode/umachine.h"`, which needs `lib/src` on the include path; both builds add only `lib/include`. gcc and clang look for a quoted include beside the header that includes it (`lib/src/unicode/`), then on the path, then in the system headers. So:
- **macOS** built by taking Apple's ICU header from the SDK (`MacOSX.sdk/usr/include/unicode/umachine.h`) instead of tree-sitter's — wrong, silently;
- **Linux** has no ICU headers unless `libicu-dev` is installed, so it fails;
- **Windows** built because MSVC also searches the directory of the file that started the include chain (`lib.c`, in `lib/src`).

Add `lib/src` to the include path for tree-sitter's `lib.c` only (as tree-sitter's own build does), in CMake and the Makefile, so its headers cannot shadow kb's.

**Done when:** on macOS, `lib.c` compiles against the vendored `umachine.h`, not the SDK's (checked with `-H`); kb's suites pass; the user's Linux build succeeds.

item.title: lap: chunked history and branches in other folders
item.description:
Agents cannot work in parallel on one codebase today: lap has one history, one active session, and files on disk are shared. The design discussed with the user on 2026-09-27:

- **Chunks.** The log becomes a directory of chunk files, ordered by the hash chain (a chunk's first record's `prev` is the previous chunk's last hash). A chunk is sealed at a size limit or when a branch starts from it, and never written again. Existing logs split losslessly (no record or hash changes).
- **Branches.** A branch is a lap repository in another folder (a git worktree or a plain copy) whose history shares its parent's up to a base hash. `lap branch start [name] --from <parent>`. With branches, a commit must name its target.
- **Merge = adopt.** git merges the code; `lap merge` adopts the branch's commits into the parent's history with a three-way offset mapping (base / parent / branch), per file, stopping a file at its first conflict. What is left is committed by hand. Adopted commits get the parent's ids and a `from` link.
- **Registry.** The parent records where its branches live (`.lap/branches.json`, machine-local). It is hints, never errors: merged-and-gone branches are pruned silently; unmerged-and-gone ones are shown as missing.
- **The board is not branched**: agents in branch folders write to the parent's board.
- Views show branches.

The SPEC comes first, as a draft reviewed by the user, then chunks, then branches.

item.title: lap CLI: history stored as chunks
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Chunks (layout, why sealing, what changes elsewhere). Only the `main` lineage exists in this ticket; branches come in M-11, but nothing here may assume a single lineage in the file format.

**Goal.** lap reads and writes its history as `.lap/log/main.<n>.jsonl` instead of `.lap/log.jsonl`, with no change to any record or hash.

**Build**
- Chunk files `<lineage>.<n>.jsonl`, `n` zero-padded to 6 digits, from 1. The open chunk is the highest `n` of a lineage; lower ones are sealed and never written.
- Sealing: an append that would take the open chunk past 4 MB starts chunk `n+1`; a single record over 4 MB is a chunk of its own. The limit is a constant (`LAP_CHUNK_BYTES` in `lap.h`); tests need small chunks, so honour an environment override `LAP_TEST_CHUNK_BYTES`, and say in the SPEC that it exists for tests only.
- Reading a history: a lineage's chunks in `n` order, the chain continuous across them (a chunk's first `prev` = the previous chunk's last hash). `rec_log_load` and everything that reads "the log" (heal, replay, verify, search, rr, hash lookup) go through this.
- Torn tail: only in the open chunk; readers drop it, writers truncate it under the lock (today's rules, per chunk).
- Index (`idx.h`): entries point at (chunk, offset) instead of an offset into one file — it is a cache, change its format freely and bump its magic.
- `lap verify`: walks the chain across chunks; a break inside a sealed chunk is reported as `sealed chunk <name> was modified`.
- `Repo.logpath` and `LAP_LOG_NAME` give way to the log directory; nothing may still read `log.jsonl` except the conversion (T-105).

**Traps**

item.title: Existing logs convert to chunks by themselves; git and the skills follow

Under the lock; a crash midway must leave either the old file or a complete set of chunks usable (write chunks first, remove the old file last; a leftover `log.jsonl` next to complete chunks is removed on the next writer).

item.title: lap branch start: a folder becomes a branch of another
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Terms, §Chunks, §Branches → Starting one. Blocked by M-10 (T-104, T-105).

**Goal.** In a folder made by `git worktree add` or by copying the parent folder, `lap branch start [name] --from <parent folder>` makes it a branch: its history is the parent's up to a base hash, then its own.

**Build**
- Lineage-aware history: a folder's history = its parent's history up to the base (recursively, down to `main`), then its own lineage's chunks. The `branch` record (`{"type":"branch","id","name","parent","base","user","ts","prev"=base}`) is the first record of the lineage's first chunk and is how lap knows a folder's lineage, parent and base.
- The command, in order (SPEC steps 1–5): copy the parent's chunks (no `.lap/`) or check this folder's head is in the parent's history (copied folder) → `unrelated_history`; check every tracked file equals this folder's committed state → `not_clean` listing files; under the **parent's** lock, seal the parent's open chunk (create its empty `n+1`) and copy the sealed version here; write the branch record; add the registry entry (T-108 builds the registry; this ticket can write the entry through the function T-108 provides, or land a minimal writer T-108 then owns).
- Branch id: first 12 hex of SHA-256(base ‖ name ‖ time ‖ random nonce); `name` optional, defaults to the id. Names must be unique among the parent's branches.
- Ids continue the parent's `L`/`S` counters from the base.
- Refuse when the parent cannot be written (read-only), without leaving anything half-made in either folder.
- A branch of a branch: same command, `--from` a branch folder.

**Traps**
- Sealing is not optional: in a git worktree the branch folder's chunks are as git last committed them; without sealing, the parent keeps appending to a chunk the branch also changed, and `git merge` conflicts on it (SPEC §Why a branch start seals…).
- `lap` never writes tracked files (core rule 4): copying chunks writes only under `.lap/`.

**Done when**
- e2e, with real `git worktree add` and with a plain `cp -R`: start a branch, commit in both folders, `git merge` the worktree's git branch into the parent — **no git conflict in `.lap/log/`**; a branch of a branch; `unrelated_history`, `not_clean` and a read-only parent refused cleanly;
- `lap verify` passes in both folders; the parent's history is unchanged apart from the sealing;
- `SPEC.md` holds §Branches → Starting one and the core-rule changes it needs.

item.title: The branch registry: where branches live, as hints
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Registry and §Commands. Works with T-107 (which adds entries).

**Goal.** The parent knows where its branch folders are, for `lap merge` and the views — and never fails because of it.

**Build**
- `.lap/branches.json`: `[{id, name, path (absolute), base, started}]`, machine-local, not committed, written atomically under the lock.
- Checked, never trusted: an entry counts only if its folder exists and that folder's `.lap` is that branch (by the `branch` record's id).
- Pruning, by writers only: an entry whose branch was merged up to its head (T-112's merge record says so) and whose folder is gone is dropped silently. Unmerged or stopped-at-a-conflict and gone: kept, reported as `missing`.
- `lap branch list [--json]`: each branch's state (`active`, `merged`, `partly merged`, `missing`), commits since base and since the last merge, last known path. In a branch folder, also its own name, parent and base.
- `lap branch forget <branch>`, `lap branch move <branch> <path>` (the new path must hold that branch).
- No command fails because of the registry; the one error is `lap merge` finding the branch nowhere (T-112).

**Done when**
- e2e: a deleted unmerged branch shows as `missing` and `forget` removes it; `move` repoints a moved folder; a folder reused for something else is not taken for the branch; a deleted **merged** branch disappears on the next writing command without a message (with a stand-in merge record until T-112 lands, then with a real merge);
- `branch list --json` shape documented in `SPEC.md` (§Registry, §Commands moved from the draft).

item.description:

item.title: Adoption: place a branch's commits on the parent's version of a file
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Merging (the per-file walk, offsets, conflict). Can start before M-11 is done: it is pure logic.

**Goal.** The algorithm at the heart of `lap merge`, as a pure module with unit tests, before any command uses it.

**Input:** the file at the branch's base (lines), the parent's current version (lines), and the branch's commits to that file in order (each a region: `old_start`, `old_lines`, `old_text`, `new_text`, in the branch's coordinates at that point). **Output:** for each commit, either its region translated to the parent's coordinates (and the parent's text after it), or a conflict — after which the rest of that file's commits are not placed.

**Rules**
- The parent's changes are the diff base → parent (lap's own `diff.c`).
- A branch commit whose region neither overlaps nor touches a parent change moves by the net lines the parent added or removed above it; each placed commit shifts the ones after it.
- Overlap is a conflict. **Touching** is a conflict too: both sides insert at the same point, or one inserts right at the edge of the other's change — either order would be a guess.
- A placed commit's `old_text` must equal the parent's text at the translated position; if it does not, that is a conflict (defensive: it means the mapping is wrong).

**Done when**
- unit tests (in `tests/unit/`): the user's example (parent adds an import at line 4, branch inserts a function at 51 → placed at 52); parent change below the branch's (no shift); deletions on the parent above; several branch commits shifting each other; overlap; both inserting at one point; touching at an edge; a pure insertion at the very top and bottom of a file; CRLF-free comparison as in `file_diff_load`;
- the module has no I/O and does not allocate beyond its arena.

item.title: lap merge: adopt a branch into the parent's history
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Merging, §Registry. Blocked by T-107, T-108, T-111.

**Goal.** After `git merge` brought a branch's code into the parent folder, `lap merge <branch> [--dry-run]` brings its history: every commit that can be placed, per file, with what is left shown by `lap status`.

**Build**
- Find the branch's chunks in this folder (a `git merge` brought them) or in its registered folder; else `branch_not_found`. Its base must be in this folder's history, else `unrelated_history`. A branch of a branch whose parent was adopted: resolve its base through the adopted commits' `from` links; if its parent's adoption stopped before that base, refuse and say so.
- Per file, run T-111's placement on: the base version (this history replayed to the base), the parent's shadow, and the branch's commits to that file after the last merge's `head`. Files stopped by an earlier merge of this branch stay stopped.
- Append, under the lock, in the branch's order: each placed commit as an ordinary commit with the next `L` id, translated coordinates, and `"from":"<branch commit hash>"`; each branch session as a new session (new `S` id, same purpose and **meta**, `from`), so `lap session list --meta ticket=T-12` still finds the work. Update shadows as commits do. Never write the working tree.
- Close with the merge record: `{"type":"merge","branch","name","head","adopted","left","stopped":[{"file","at"}],"user","ts","prev"}`.
- Report: adopted N of M; each stopped file and the first commit not adopted; then `lap status` shows the rest to commit by hand.
- `--dry-run`: the report, nothing written.
- Refuse with `branch_required`-style clarity when run in a branch folder against itself, or when the branch is this folder's own parent.

**Done when**
- e2e with real git worktrees: (1) disjoint files → everything adopted, `lap status` clean after; (2) the user's example (import on the parent, function on the branch, same file) → adopted with the shifted line, clean after; (3) a real conflict → that file stops at the right commit, other files adopted, `lap status` shows the resolution to commit, which is committed citing the branch hashes; (4) a second merge after more branch work adopts only the new commits and keeps the stopped file stopped; (5) `--dry-run` writes nothing;
- `lap verify --deep` passes in the parent after each; `lap show` on an adopted commit shows its `from` link;
- `SPEC.md` holds §Merging; `SPEC-branches.md` is down to what the views still need.

item.title: SPEC draft amendments from the design review
item.description:
The review of `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` (2026-09-27, before building) found gaps. Fold them into the draft before M-10/M-11 build on it:

1. **Base and clean files.** The base is the parent's head at `branch start`; a folder whose files are not the parent head's state is `not_clean`, and the error says why (git HEAD behind lap's head; files lap tracks that git ignores). Recommend the layout where agents work in branches and the first folder only merges.
2. **Merge keeps the originals.** `lap merge` copies the branch's chunks (up to what it adopted) into the parent's `.lap/log/` when they are not there, so `from` links and `#hash` references survive the branch folder's removal.
3. **Ids across folders.** Ids in two folders can repeat; board comments cite hashes or `<branch>/S<n>`.
4. **Sessions on adoption.** An adopted session never becomes the parent's active session; a later merge adds to the session already adopted (by `from`); `session_end` is carried when the branch ended it; adopted messages are copied as they are, not re-checked.
5. **An empty open chunk is not sealed again.** Base is then the last record of the chunk before.
6. **The branch record names its base chunk** (`base_chunk`), and a folder's lineage is kept in machine-local `.lap/lineage`.
7. **`LAP_BRANCH`** environment variable is accepted where `--branch` is.
8. **No branch of a branch in this version.**
9. The diff effort cap makes a heavily rewritten parent file one change: its branch commits conflict.

**Done when:** the draft says all of the above; the affected tickets (T-107, T-109, T-112) are updated to match.

item.title: lap CLI: history stored as chunks
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Chunks (layout, why sealing, what changes elsewhere). Only the `main` lineage exists in this ticket; branches come in M-11, but nothing here may assume a single lineage in the file format.

**Goal.** lap reads and writes its history as `.lap/log/main.<n>.jsonl` instead of `.lap/log.jsonl`, with no change to any record or hash.

**Build**
- Chunk files `<lineage>.<n>.jsonl`, `n` zero-padded to 6 digits, from 1. The open chunk is the highest `n` of a lineage; lower ones are sealed and never written.
- Sealing: an append that would take the open chunk past 4 MB starts chunk `n+1`; a single record over 4 MB is a chunk of its own. The limit is a constant (`LAP_CHUNK_BYTES` in `lap.h`); tests need small chunks, so honour an environment override `LAP_TEST_CHUNK_BYTES`, and say in the SPEC that it exists for tests only.
- Reading a history: a lineage's chunks in `n` order, the chain continuous across them (a chunk's first `prev` = the previous chunk's last hash). `rec_log_load` and everything that reads "the log" (heal, replay, verify, search, rr, hash lookup) go through this.
- Torn tail: only in the open chunk; readers drop it, writers truncate it under the lock (today's rules, per chunk).
- Index (`idx.h`): entries point at (chunk, offset) instead of an offset into one file — it is a cache, change its format freely and bump its magic.
- `lap verify`: walks the chain across chunks; a break inside a sealed chunk is reported as `sealed chunk <name> was modified`.
- `Repo.logpath` and `LAP_LOG_NAME` give way to the log directory; nothing may still read `log.jsonl` except the conversion (T-105).

**Traps**
- `tests/e2e/run.sh` reads and tampers with `.lap/log.jsonl` in ~20 places (`wc -c`, `tail -1`, forged collisions, torn-tail appends). Give the suite one helper for "the open chunk" and "the whole history in order" and move every such line to it; do not weaken what a test checks.
- The stat cache, the per-file scratch arena and the missing-shadow replay (T-97, T-99) must keep their memory behaviour: re-measure `lap status` on a cache-less typec clone (see T-99's comment for the method) and compare.

**Done when**
- lap never creates or reads `.lap/log.jsonl` (except T-105's conversion);
- e2e covers: sealing at the limit (with the test override), a chain across three chunks, a torn tail in the open chunk, `verify` naming a modified sealed chunk;
- unit and e2e suites pass; typec clone `status` timings are in the closing comment next to T-99's;
- `SPEC.md` holds §Chunks (moved from the draft, which keeps the rest).

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S105 (L2998–L3101), git `aeb3548` + `81449ed`.

**What changed**
- New module `src/hist.{h,c}`: a folder's history is the chunk files of `.lap/log/` (`<lineage>.<n>.jsonl`) read as one stream. Offsets are positions in that stream; only the open chunk grows, so the index keeps plain offsets (magic bumped to `LAPIDX02`). It lists a lineage's chunks (refusing a gap, naming the missing chunk), reads ranges across chunk boundaries straight into one buffer, hashes the last complete record (past an empty or torn-only open chunk), repairs a torn tail in the open chunk, appends with sealing at the limit (a record bigger than the limit is a chunk of its own), and seals explicitly (a no-op on an empty open chunk — ready for `branch start`). Chunks of other lineages are not listed.
- `Repo` holds the `Hist` (listed after the lock for writers); `repo_log_load` replaces every `rec_log_load(path)`; `rec_log_parse` parses bytes in memory and names positions through a callback, only when a message needs one ("main.000002.jsonl line 7").
- A chain break is blamed on the chunk before the breaking record (the changed record is the one whose hash no longer matches); if that chunk is sealed, the error is `sealed chunk main.000002.jsonl was modified: …`.
- `LAP_CHUNK_BYTES` (4 MB) in `lap.h`; `LAP_TEST_CHUNK_BYTES` overrides it, noted as test-only in SPEC. `Hist.limit` lets unit tests set it directly.

item.title: lap CLI: history stored as chunks
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Chunks (layout, why sealing, what changes elsewhere). Only the `main` lineage exists in this ticket; branches come in M-11, but nothing here may assume a single lineage in the file format.

**Goal.** lap reads and writes its history as `.lap/log/main.<n>.jsonl` instead of `.lap/log.jsonl`, with no change to any record or hash.

**Build**
- Chunk files `<lineage>.<n>.jsonl`, `n` zero-padded to 6 digits, from 1. The open chunk is the highest `n` of a lineage; lower ones are sealed and never written.
- Sealing: an append that would take the open chunk past 4 MB starts chunk `n+1`; a single record over 4 MB is a chunk of its own. The limit is a constant (`LAP_CHUNK_BYTES` in `lap.h`); tests need small chunks, so honour an environment override `LAP_TEST_CHUNK_BYTES`, and say in the SPEC that it exists for tests only.
- Reading a history: a lineage's chunks in `n` order, the chain continuous across them (a chunk's first `prev` = the previous chunk's last hash). `rec_log_load` and everything that reads "the log" (heal, replay, verify, search, rr, hash lookup) go through this.
- Torn tail: only in the open chunk; readers drop it, writers truncate it under the lock (today's rules, per chunk).
- Index (`idx.h`): entries point at (chunk, offset) instead of an offset into one file — it is a cache, change its format freely and bump its magic.
- `lap verify`: walks the chain across chunks; a break inside a sealed chunk is reported as `sealed chunk <name> was modified`.
- `Repo.logpath` and `LAP_LOG_NAME` give way to the log directory; nothing may still read `log.jsonl` except the conversion (T-105).

- `tests/e2e/run.sh` reads and tampers with `.lap/log.jsonl` in ~20 places (`wc -c`, `tail -1`, forged collisions, torn-tail appends). Give the suite one helper for "the open chunk" and "the whole history in order" and move every such line to it; do not weaken what a test checks.

item.title: Lap History reads chunked history
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Chunks. Blocked by T-104. Must land with T-104/T-105, or the view goes blank on a converted repository.

**Goal.** Lap History keeps working after the log becomes `.lap/log/`.

`packages/lap-vscode` does not ask the lap CLI for history: it parses the log file itself (`src/model.ts`, `src/extension.ts` around the `logPath`), watches it (`**/.lap/log.jsonl`), and activates on `workspaceContains:.lap/log.jsonl` (also merged into the combined extension's manifest by `packages/combined/scripts/build.mjs`).

- Activation: `workspaceContains:.lap/log` plus the old event, so both shapes activate.
- Keep incremental refresh cheap: only the open chunk grows; sealed chunks never change.

**Done when**
- unit tests: a history split over several chunks parses to the same commits and sessions as the single file; an unconverted repository still parses;
- the view renders on a converted scratch clone of typec (light and dark theme);

item.title: lap branch start: a folder becomes a branch of another
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Terms, §Chunks, §Branches → Starting one. Blocked by M-10 (T-104, T-105).

**Goal.** In a folder made by `git worktree add` or by copying the parent folder, `lap branch start [name] --from <parent folder>` makes it a branch: its history is the parent's up to a base hash, then its own.

**Build**
- Lineage-aware history: a folder's history = its parent's history up to the base (recursively, down to `main`), then its own lineage's chunks. The `branch` record (`{"type":"branch","id","name","parent","base","user","ts","prev"=base}`) is the first record of the lineage's first chunk and is how lap knows a folder's lineage, parent and base.
- The command, in order (SPEC steps 1–5): copy the parent's chunks (no `.lap/`) or check this folder's head is in the parent's history (copied folder) → `unrelated_history`; check every tracked file equals this folder's committed state → `not_clean` listing files; under the **parent's** lock, seal the parent's open chunk (create its empty `n+1`) and copy the sealed version here; write the branch record; add the registry entry (T-108 builds the registry; this ticket can write the entry through the function T-108 provides, or land a minimal writer T-108 then owns).
- Branch id: first 12 hex of SHA-256(base ‖ name ‖ time ‖ random nonce); `name` optional, defaults to the id. Names must be unique among the parent's branches.
- Ids continue the parent's `L`/`S` counters from the base.
- Refuse when the parent cannot be written (read-only), without leaving anything half-made in either folder.
- A branch of a branch: same command, `--from` a branch folder.

**Traps**
- Sealing is not optional: in a git worktree the branch folder's chunks are as git last committed them; without sealing, the parent keeps appending to a chunk the branch also changed, and `git merge` conflicts on it (SPEC §Why a branch start seals…).
- `lap` never writes tracked files (core rule 4): copying chunks writes only under `.lap/`.

**Done when**
- e2e, with real `git worktree add` and with a plain `cp -R`: start a branch, commit in both folders, `git merge` the worktree's git branch into the parent — **no git conflict in `.lap/log/`**; a branch of a branch; `unrelated_history`, `not_clean` and a read-only parent refused cleanly;
- `lap verify` passes in both folders; the parent's history is unchanged apart from the sealing;
- `SPEC.md` holds §Branches → Starting one and the core-rule changes it needs.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S108 (L3144–L3192), git `87ea92f` + `8d599ec`.

**What changed**
- **Branch record** (`REC_BRANCH`): `{"type":"branch","id","name","parent","base","base_chunk","user","ts","prev"=base}`, indexed (`IDX_BRANCH`); the state heal and the index clear the open session at it, so a branch starts with none.
- **Branch-aware history** (`hist_open_folder`): `.lap/lineage` (machine-local) names the folder's lineage, default `main`; a branch folder's history is the parent's chunks `1..base_chunk`, then its own, and appends go only to its own chunk. `repo_open` uses it; `repo_open_at` opens a repository at a given root (how a branch reaches its parent); `repo_abspath` resolves `--from`.
- **Registry** (`branches.{h,c}`): `.lap/branches.json` as hints — a missing or malformed file reads as empty, incomplete entries are skipped. T-108 adds list/forget/move and the pruning rules.
- **`lap branch start [name] --from <folder>`** (`cmd_branch.c`), holding the parent's lock throughout: name and folder checks; refuses `already_branch`, `same_folder`, `no_parent`, `nested_branch`; this folder's history (chunks or single-file log) must be a byte prefix of the parent's (`unrelated_history`); every file must equal the parent's committed state, compared as status does (`not_clean`, listing up to 20 files and naming both usual causes); `name_taken`; then seals the parent's open chunk (no-op when it is empty), registers the branch in the parent **before** writing anything here (`parent_read_only`), copies the parent's chunks up to the base, drops a copied registry, writes the branch record and `.lap/lineage`, and builds caches.
- **Found on the way:** in a git worktree `.git` is a *file*, which lap reported as a new file (and which made every worktree `not_clean`). `.git` is now ignored as a file or a directory (ignore.c, SPEC's .lapignore section, a unit test).
- `SPEC.md`: core rules 4 and 6, the layout (`lineage`, `branches.json`), per-folder linear history, the branch record, a new §Branches (lineages, ids from the base, no session, no nesting, Starting one in five steps, names and ids, the recommended layout, §Registry as hints), and the command with its errors. The draft points there.

**Tests:** unit 4,015 (new: branch record round trip and refusal; lineage file default/validation/write; a branch history read as parent chunks then its own; appends staying in the branch's chunk; missing base chunk and missing branch record refused; the registry: missing, round trip, lookup, malformed and partial). e2e 109, new scenarios (git present): a real `git worktree add` start (record first, `base_chunk`, parent chunk sealed and unchanged byte for byte, registry entry, no session, verify --deep); ids going on from the base in both folders; **`git merge` of the worktree branch into the parent with no conflict in `.lap/log/`**, the parent's chain still whole and the merged edit pending in its status; a second branch sharing the base with no new seal; a plain `cp -R` of the parent (caches and all) becoming a branch; every refusal, with nothing left behind; a read-only parent (skipped when run as root).

**Not done here, by design:** a branch of a branch (refused, per T-118). Found while testing: two repositories initialised in the same second have byte-identical `init` records, so a folder holding only that record passes the prefix check. That is literally a shared history, so it is left as is; the e2e test gives the unrelated folder a record of its own.

**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Merging (the per-file walk, offsets, conflict). Can start before M-11 is done: it is pure logic.

**Goal.** The algorithm at the heart of `lap merge`, as a pure module with unit tests, before any command uses it.

**Input:** the file at the branch's base (lines), the parent's current version (lines), and the branch's commits to that file in order (each a region: `old_start`, `old_lines`, `old_text`, `new_text`, in the branch's coordinates at that point). **Output:** for each commit, either its region translated to the parent's coordinates (and the parent's text after it), or a conflict — after which the rest of that file's commits are not placed.

**Rules**
- The parent's changes are the diff base → parent (lap's own `diff.c`).
- A branch commit whose region neither overlaps nor touches a parent change moves by the net lines the parent added or removed above it; each placed commit shifts the ones after it.
- Overlap is a conflict. **Touching** is a conflict too: both sides insert at the same point, or one inserts right at the edge of the other's change — either order would be a guess.
- A placed commit's `old_text` must equal the parent's text at the translated position; if it does not, that is a conflict (defensive: it means the mapping is wrong).

**Done when**
- unit tests (in `tests/unit/`): the user's example (parent adds an import at line 4, branch inserts a function at 51 → placed at 52); parent change below the branch's (no shift); deletions on the parent above; several branch commits shifting each other; overlap; both inserting at one point; touching at an edge; a pure insertion at the very top and bottom of a file; CRLF-free comparison as in `file_diff_load`;
- the module has no I/O and does not allocate beyond its arena.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S110 (L3219–L3230), git `da211c0`. From this session on, edits are made one at a time with the Edit tool, each followed by its own lap commit (the user's rule; scripted edits only for rare mechanical changes).

**What changed**
- `src/adopt.{h,c}`: `adopt_place(base, parent, commits[], n) → Placement {placed, start[], eof_nl[], result, why}`. Pure: no I/O; everything in the caller's arena.
  - The parent's changes are `diff_lines(base, parent)` (CR-blind), kept as intervals in the branch's current coordinates.
  - A branch commit `[s, s+old_lines)` conflicts when `s <= pe && ps <= e` for any parent change `[ps, pe)` — this covers overlap, both inserting at one point, and touching at either edge. Otherwise it moves by the net lines of the parent changes wholly above it.
  - Defensive check: the commit's old text must equal the parent's lines where it lands (CR-blind), else a conflict. A delete must cover the whole of the parent's version.
  - Placed commits shift the later parent changes by their own net lines. The end-of-file newline is the commit's when the commit changed it, otherwise the parent's (so a parent that dropped the final newline keeps that through unrelated branch edits).
  - The first conflict stops the file, with a reason in `why`.
- `without_cr` moved from `cmd_common.c` (static) to `str.c` as `lines_without_cr`, so the pure module can share it; `file_diff_load` calls it. No behaviour change: e2e 110 pass, CRLF scenarios included.

item.title: lap merge: adopt a branch into the parent's history
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Merging, §Registry. Blocked by T-107, T-108, T-111.

**Goal.** After `git merge` brought a branch's code into the parent folder, `lap merge <branch> [--dry-run]` brings its history: every commit that can be placed, per file, with what is left shown by `lap status`.

**Build**
- Find the branch's chunks in this folder (a `git merge` brought them) or in its registered folder; else `branch_not_found`. Its base must be in this folder's history, else `unrelated_history`. A branch of a branch whose parent was adopted: resolve its base through the adopted commits' `from` links; if its parent's adoption stopped before that base, refuse and say so.
- Per file, run T-111's placement on: the base version (this history replayed to the base), the parent's shadow, and the branch's commits to that file after the last merge's `head`. Files stopped by an earlier merge of this branch stay stopped.
- Append, under the lock, in the branch's order: each placed commit as an ordinary commit with the next `L` id, translated coordinates, and `"from":"<branch commit hash>"`; each branch session as a new session (new `S` id, same purpose and **meta**, `from`), so `lap session list --meta ticket=T-12` still finds the work. Update shadows as commits do. Never write the working tree.
- Close with the merge record: `{"type":"merge","branch","name","head","adopted","left","stopped":[{"file","at"}],"user","ts","prev"}`.
- Report: adopted N of M; each stopped file and the first commit not adopted; then `lap status` shows the rest to commit by hand.
- `--dry-run`: the report, nothing written.
- Refuse with `branch_required`-style clarity when run in a branch folder against itself, or when the branch is this folder's own parent.

**Done when**
- e2e with real git worktrees: (1) disjoint files → everything adopted, `lap status` clean after; (2) the user's example (import on the parent, function on the branch, same file) → adopted with the shifted line, clean after; (3) a real conflict → that file stops at the right commit, other files adopted, `lap status` shows the resolution to commit, which is committed citing the branch hashes; (4) a second merge after more branch work adopts only the new commits and keeps the stopped file stopped; (5) `--dry-run` writes nothing;
- `lap verify --deep` passes in the parent after each; `lap show` on an adopted commit shows its `from` link;
- `SPEC.md` holds §Merging; `SPEC-branches.md` is down to what the views still need.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S111 (L3231–L3269), git `547d659`.

**What changed**
- **Records:** `from` (the original's hash) on adopted commits, session starts and ends; a new `merge` record (`branch`, `name`, `head`, `adopted`, `left`, `stopped:[{file,at}]`, `user`). Adopted records keep the branch's `ts` and `user` (`repo_append` only stamps a record that has no time). The state heal and the index count adopted sessions' ids but never make one active, nor let an adopted end close the folder's own session.
- **`hist_open_lineage`** (split out of `hist_open_folder`) reads a branch lineage from the chunks a folder holds; **`hist_lineages`** lists the branch lineages present.
- **`lap merge <branch> [--dry-run] [--json]`** (`cmd_merge.c`):
  1. finds the branch by registry or by chunks present;
  2. when its folder is reachable, seals its open chunk under its lock and copies its chunks here;
  3. checks the base;
  4. resumes after the last merge's `head`;
  5. per file, runs `adopt_place` (T-111) against the branch's version at that head and this folder's version now; stopped files stay stopped;
  6. appends new sessions, placed commits and session ends in the branch's order, with `from` links; an already adopted session is reused;
  7. closes with the merge record, updates shadows (never the working tree), and reports.

  `--dry-run` reads the branch folder in place and writes nothing. Errors: `branch_not_found`, `merge_in_branch`, `unrelated_history`, `log_broken`.
- **`lap show`** prints `from: #<short> (adopted … the original is <hash>)`; `from` is in every command's commit JSON.
- `SPEC.md`: record types, §Branches → Merging (five steps, what is left, dry run), the command. The draft points there. The lap skill says how to merge back.

**Tests:** unit 4,106 (new: merge record round trip; `from` on commits, session starts and ends; the effort cap — a parent file rewritten with 1,499 changes diffs as one truncated change, so a branch insertion in it conflicts). e2e 116, on real git worktrees unless said:
1. disjoint files → both adopted as L6, L7; `--dry-run` left `.lap/` byte-identical; `status` clean; the parent's own open session still current; `session list --meta ticket=T-7` finds the adopted session; `show` prints `from`; `verify --deep` ok; a second merge says nothing new.
2. The import-and-function example → adopted at lines 52–53, `status` clean.
3. A real git conflict → `f.txt` stops at the line-10 commit (checked against its hash in the output and the merge record), line 50 and `g.txt` adopted; `status` shows exactly 2 edits left, committed by hand citing the stopped commit's hash; clean after; `verify --deep` ok.
4. A second merge after more work → adopts only the new `g.txt` commit; `f.txt` stays stopped.
5. A plain `cp -R` branch with no git: `lap merge` seals the copy's chunk there and copies it here; the copy folder is deleted and the parent still verifies and knows there is nothing new.
6. The refusals.

**Left to T-113:** `lap show <original hash>` from the parent (hash lookups across lineages) and `verify` walking every lineage present. **Left to T-108:** pruning merged-and-gone registry entries and `branch list` states, now that merge records exist.

item.title: Reading another branch's history: --branch on log, show and rr
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Commands (the `--branch` reading bullet). Blocked by T-107, T-108.

**Goal.** From the parent folder, review a branch's work before or after merging it.

**Build**
- `lap log`, `lap show`, `lap rr` take `--branch <name>` to read another lineage present in this folder (a merged-in branch's chunks) or in a registered branch folder. Without the flag, they read this folder's own lineage, as now.
- `lap show <hash>` finds a commit in any lineage present, so an adopted commit's `from` link can be followed; the output says which branch it belongs to.
- `--json` outputs carry the lineage (`branch`) of each commit.

**Done when**
- e2e: log/show/rr of a branch from its parent, before and after `git merge` brought its chunks; following a `from` link with `show`;
- `SPEC.md` documents the flag and the JSON field.
